provenance.method: Hand-authored offline evidence pack modeling the documented OpenCode 1.17.18 CLI, NDJSON transport, and debug/export JSON contract. No live OpenCode process, network access, or real provider/model was used; every fixture is a static, version-pinned test double checked into the repository.

corrections.reason: The M07-01 pack's seven debug/agent-*.json fixtures modeled `debug agent <role>` with a flat `permission: {edit, bash, webfetch}` dict and a `tools.ask` boolean -- an assumption never checked against a real binary. Live qualification against a real, locally installed 1.17.18 binary showed the actual response uses `tools.question` (not `tools.ask`, which never appears at all) and an ordered `permission: [{permission, action, pattern}, ...]` rule list resolved last-match-wins (https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), not a flat dict. All seven fixtures were corrected to the real shape and re-hashed; `src/opencode_tools/opencode.py`'s check_debug_agent and run --help's stdout/stderr capture were corrected to match.

decode_run_transport assumed `opencode run --format json` wraps every message part in a `message.part.updated` envelope -- an assumption never checked against a real binary. A live re-qualification run (after fixing the earlier model-resolution blocker) captured a genuine NDJSON transcript and proved this wrong: real 1.17.18 output carries the message-lifecycle kind directly as the top-level `type` (`step_start`, `text`, `step_finish`, `tool_use`, `reasoning`, `error`), never wrapped. Every attempt was failing PROTOCOL_ERROR even when the agent's final message carried a syntactically valid AGENT_STATUS marker, because the parser never recognized the real event type and so never read it. `_ALLOWED_TRANSPORT_EVENT_TYPES` and `decode_run_transport` were corrected to the real contract (no `message.part.updated` fallback), `run/architect-failed.ndjson` was replaced with the genuine captured transcript, and the remaining run/provider/malformed NDJSON fixtures were converted from the unproven envelope shape to the real one.

A live re-qualification run (after the transport-shape fix above) reached a genuine, correctly-parsed architect response for the first time and exposed a real, pre-existing design contradiction: `build_architect_prompt` instructs the architect to run `gh issue view` itself to discover the issue title/body (Python never reads or embeds them -- ADR-007/FR-017), but `.opencode/agents/architect.md` declared `bash: deny` outright, so the architect had no tool to ever run that command -- every honest run was destined to report AGENT_STATUS: FAILED. Fixed with least privilege, not a broader flat allow: the architect's bash permission is now a config-time nested object (`_ARCHITECT_BASH_PERMISSION_CONFIG`) denying everything by default except the single, exact `gh issue view *` pattern its own prompt names. `check_debug_agent` now verifies this via `_check_architect_bash_policy`, which simulates OpenCode's real last-match-wins glob resolution against representative probe commands rather than comparing a literal rule list, because a live capture showed a machine's own global OpenCode config can legitimately prepend an unrelated catch-all rule that a literal-shape comparison would trip over.

AC-027 live re-qualification PASSED twice, independently, against a disposable private GitHub repository and a controlled issue on this project's own macOS (darwin) development machine, using the real, project-local architect/coder/reviewer agent definitions and their own configured openrouter provider/model with zero fallback. Both runs: exact version 1.17.18, verified_agent matching the requested role for every attempt via sanitized export, three distinct session_id values, git_safety_status SAFE, no remote/local HEAD or commit-count change, final_status APPROVED. compatibility_status moves from 'candidate' to 'supported' per ADR-005's three-step gate; the corresponding prose lives in docs/compatibility.md.
